newsitem.title: USA: Firm files for stay of Chicago exchange sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Firm files for stay of Chicago exchange sanctions.

text.p: Chicago-based stock brokerage Scattered Corp has filed an application with the Securities and Exchange Commission for a stay of sanctions imposed on it by the Chicago Stock Exchange, Leon Greenblatt, the firm's head trader, said Tuesday.
"We've appealed to the SEC for a stay of the sanctions, which we believe will be granted," Greenblatt said in a telephone interview.
"We filed an initial application for a stay today and will do a permanent application sometime next week," he said.

Earlier Tuesday, the exchange said its executive committee had affirmed a July 1996 decision of its judiciary committee sanctioning Scattered Corp, three of its principals and its trading floor nominee.

The exchange alleged the brokerage firm and the four individuals had violated "numerous" provisions of the U.S. Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and various exchange rules through illegal short sales, price manipulation, failure to keep adequate records, abuse of position as market maker and excessive trading.

The exchange's hearing examiner in 1995 handed down a judgment against Scattered Corp and the individuals that included fines of $6.83 million, revocation of the firm's membership and various suspensions for the individuals.
After the judiciary committee upheld the hearing examiner's decision, Scattered Corp and the individuals appealed to the executive committee, which ruled Tuesday.

The disciplinary hearing and appeals arose primarily from trading by the firm and individuals in common stock of steelmaker LTV Corp in mid-1993. ((Derivatives desk, 3124088750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
